collected_dynamic_variables.interest_topic: this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets

transcript:
User: Yeah I saw your thing online. Honestly this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets. Convince me it's not garbage.
Agent: Totally fair reaction — there’s a lot of junk out there right now.  

Before I try to “convince” you of anything… when you say “AI scam gadgets,” what kind of garbage have you seen before — robocalls, fake assistants, tools nobody on your team actually uses?
User: Exactly, robocalls and those fake assistants. How do I know this isn't just another one of those?
Agent: Yeah, makes sense — those robocalls trained everyone to be suspicious.  

Let me ask you this: when a real customer calls your business and nobody picks up — it rings out or hits voicemail — what usually happens next for them?
User: They probably hang up and call the next roofing company. How do I know this isn't a recording?
Agent: Got it, so if you miss them, they just move on to the next roofer — that’s exactly where money leaks out.  

Yeah, I’m an AI assistant on Jay’s team at Dialux, not a static recording — but more important than me is your phone: how often do you think that “hang up and call the next roofer” thing happens in a typical week?
User: About 30 calls a week, I'd say. But who sees my data if I work with you?
Agent: Mhm, about 30 a week — that adds up fast if they’re rolling to the next roofer.  

On the data side, Dialux only uses your call info to answer your customers and book work for you — we don’t sell or share it, and access is limited to our team running your account; what specifically are you most worried someone might see or misuse?
User: I just don't want random marketers or bots calling my customers. Can you guarantee that won't happen?
Agent: Totally hear you — the last thing you want is somebody spamming your customers under your name.  

What we do is only answer the calls that are already coming into your business line; we don’t cold call or market to your customers at all — when you think about those 30 missed calls a week, do you have a sense of what each booked job is usually worth to you on average?
User: Each job averages about $1,800. But how do I know I won't lose control over my business calls?
Agent: Got it, control’s a big deal — it’s your name on every call.  

If you booked even 50% of those 30 missed calls at $1,800, that’s about $27,000 extra a week just from answering — if you could keep control while recovering that kind of money, would it be worth exploring how our system actually works?
User: $27,000 sounds tempting, but I'm not convinced yet. How do I stay in control without risking my reputation?
Agent: Makes sense — your name and reputation are worth way more than any tech.  

So… if every call our system answered was fully recorded, you could listen anytime, and you set the rules for what it can and can’t say (plus you can turn it off anytime) — would that feel like you’re still in the driver’s seat?
User: Recorded calls and control sound better, but I need to know who else sees or uses the recordings.
Agent: Yeah, totally fair — recordings are only helpful if you know exactly who can access them.  

Normally it’s just your account on your side and a small, named team on our side for setup and support — would you want those recordings locked down so only you (or someone you choose) can listen, or are you okay with a couple of trusted managers having access too?
User: I'd want only me to access them, no one else. What's next if I agree to try this?
Agent: Got it — we can set it so only you have access, that’s no problem.  

Next step is a short live call where Jay walks you through exactly how it handles your calls and how you keep control — can we grab a few details so we can text you a confirmation?
User: Alright, as long as it's just a walk-through, my number's +14695550001. No spam, right?
Agent: Makes sense, and yeah — no spam, just the walk-through you agreed to.  

Since we’ve got your number, what’s your first name so I know who Jay will be speaking with?
User: Just call me Sam, but keep it strictly about the calls. No funny business.
Agent: Got it Sam, we’ll keep it strictly about handling your calls.  

And what’s the name of your roofing company?
User: Ortiz Roofing. Just make sure this call doesn't turn into some sales pitch, alright?
Agent: Totally hear you, Sam — this is about fixing missed calls, not shoving a hard pitch at you.  

Quick check — you’re on Central time, right?
User: Yeah, Central time here in Dallas. Just keep it straightforward and no surprises.
Agent: Got it, Dallas Central time, straightforward and no surprises.  

So for the walk-through with Jay, would you rather do later today or tomorrow?
User: Let's go with tomorrow. I want to make sure I have time to focus without distractions.
Agent: Makes sense, tomorrow with a clear head is better anyway.  

I can get you in tomorrow at either 10:45 am or 11:30 am Central for a straight 20‑minute walk-through with Jay, no surprises — which one works better for you?
User: 10:45 am works. Just remember, I'm cautious with this stuff. Keep it straightforward, no surprises.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for tomorrow at 10:45 am Central.
Agent: Thanks, Sam. You’re all set for tomorrow at 10:45 am Central with Jay — strictly about your calls, no surprises. You’ll get a text with the confirmation in a bit; you can save it or reschedule from there if you need to. Really glad you called in — Jay’s looking forward to walking you through how to stop losing those missed-call jobs. Have a great rest of your day, and we’ll talk tomorrow. Bye!
